body: In an ordinary chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged into different combinations. Existing bonds can change or break, and new bonds can form. Reactants are the substances taking part at the start. Products are substances formed by the reaction.

A chemical equation can count the atoms before and after a reaction. Two hydrogen molecules have four hydrogen atoms in total. One oxygen molecule has two oxygen atoms. Together they account for the atoms in two water molecules. A balanced equation conserves the number of atoms of each element.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: The counts in a balanced equation do not specify when a reaction will occur or how fast. The example describes atom accounting without forming a laboratory procedure.
purpose: Teach conservation and rearrangement of atoms before interpreting chemical processes.
